source_text: Gratiam Christi omnibus necessariam, et maioribus et parvulis, confitemur et eos qui dicunt de duobus baptizatis natum non debere baptizari, anathematizamus.
pass_a_gloss: We confess the grace of Christ necessary for all, both greater ones and little ones, and we anathematize those who say that one born from two baptized people ought not to be baptized.

lemmas.lexica: LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'
LS parvulus; Blaise infants in original-sin debate

pass_b_english: We confess that Christ's grace is necessary for everyone, adults and infants alike. We condemn those who say that a child born to two baptized parents does not need to be baptized.

choices.why: In the suum cuique definition gratia is partiality, not saving grace.
Speechless newborns without rational choice; Julian's test case against inherited sin.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (Letter to Rome, words preserved in Augustine, Contra duas epistolas Pelagianorum 1); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
